commands.name: login
commands.summary: Log the CLI in to a 5050cloud console and store an API token.
flags: Store this API token instead of opening the browser (for servers and CI)
Print the login link and code instead of opening a browser
details: Without `--token`, the CLI starts a device login: it opens `URL` in your browser, you approve the code shown in the terminal, and the CLI stores the token it receives.
Tokens live in `~/.config/5050/config.json` (mode 0600), one per console URL, so you can log in to several installs.
In CI, skip login and set `FIFTY_URL` and `FIFTY_TOKEN` instead.

commands.name: logout
commands.summary: Remove the stored token for the current console.
details: The token is deleted from `~/.config/5050/config.json`. Revoke it on the server under **Account > Tokens** if it may have leaked.

commands.name: whoami
commands.summary: Print the user and console the CLI is logged in to.
details: Exits non-zero when you are not logged in, so scripts can check it.

commands.name: init
commands.summary: Create a project and link this directory to it.
flags: Project name (asked for when omitted on a terminal)
details: Creates the project with a `production` environment and links the current directory, so later commands know where to act.
Run `5050 up --new` next to create a service from this directory.

commands.name: link
commands.summary: Link this directory to a project, environment and service.
details: With no flags on a terminal, numbered prompts let you pick each one.
Links are stored per absolute directory in `~/.config/5050/config.json`.

commands.name: unlink
commands.summary: Remove the link between this directory and a project.

commands.name: status
commands.summary: Show the linked project, environment and service, with its status and URL.
details: The status uses the same labels as the console: Initializing, Building, Deploying, Active, Crashed, Failed and so on. See [Deployment statuses](/docs/reference/deployment-statuses).

commands.name: list
commands.summary: List the projects you can see.
details: Add `--json` for a machine-readable list.

commands.name: open
commands.summary: Open the project canvas in your browser.
flags: Open the linked service's panel instead of the canvas

commands.name: up
commands.summary: Upload this directory and deploy it into the linked service, streaming the logs.
flags: Return after the upload instead of streaming logs
Stream only the build logs and exit when the build finishes; non-zero on failure
Create a new service from this directory
Name for the service created by `--new`
Use PATH as the root of the upload instead of the linked root directory
details: The CLI packs the directory as a gzipped tar, skipping `.git` and anything matched by `.gitignore` and `.5050ignore`.
Uploads over 500 MB are refused. Add large files to `.5050ignore`.
It prints `Uploaded 3.2 MB`, the build log, the first deploy log lines, then `Deployed: https://...` and exits 0. On failure it prints the one-sentence diagnosis and exits 1.

commands.name: redeploy
commands.summary: Redeploy the active deployment of the linked service.
details: Uses the same image, settings and variables as the active deployment. To pick up new commits, push or run `5050 up`.

commands.name: restart
commands.summary: Restart the active deployment's containers, one replica at a time.

commands.name: down
commands.summary: Remove the active deployment of the linked service.
details: The service stays on the canvas with "No deployment". Redeploy or push to bring it back.

commands.name: deploy
commands.summary: Add a template to the linked project and deploy it.
flags: Set a template input; generated inputs are filled in for you
details: Required inputs you do not pass are asked for on a terminal and refused in CI.

commands.name: templates
commands.summary: List or search the templates this install ships.
details: See [Templates](/docs/reference/templates) for the full list.

commands.name: add
commands.summary: Add a service: a database, a GitHub repo, a Docker image or an empty service.
flags: Add a database from its template
Add a service built from a GitHub repo
Add a service that runs a Docker image
Add an empty service to configure later
Set variables on the new service

commands.name: import
commands.summary: Import a Railway project, a Docker Compose file or Heroku variables.
flags: Railway project token (used once, never stored)
details: Imports land as staged changes in a new project (Railway) or the linked environment (Compose, Heroku). Nothing deploys until you press **Deploy** or commit.
`heroku-env` reads the output of `heroku config --json` or `heroku config -s`.
See [Import from Railway](/docs/guides/import-from-railway) and [Import Docker Compose](/docs/guides/import-docker-compose).

commands.name: logs
commands.summary: Print deploy, build or HTTP logs, following them on a terminal.
flags: The newest deployment, even if it is not active
details: Deploy logs of the active deployment are the default.

commands.name: variables
commands.summary: List, set and delete the linked service's variables.
flags: Show values (audited reveal); without it only names are listed
Read the value from standard input (for multi-line values and secrets you do not want in shell history)
Stage the change instead of committing it
details: `variable` is an alias.
`set` stages and commits in one step unless `--stage` is given. References such as `${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}` are stored as written and resolved at deploy time; quote them in your shell.

commands.name: run
commands.summary: Run a local command with the service's resolved variables.
details: Useful for migrations and scripts on your laptop. Private `.internal` hosts are not reachable from your laptop; use `5050 connect` for databases.
Sealed variables are not included.

commands.name: shell
commands.summary: Open a local subshell with the service's variables loaded.

commands.name: ssh
commands.summary: Open a shell inside a running replica.
flags: Pick a replica (default: the first running one)
Name the session so you can reattach to it within 10 minutes
details: The shell runs over a WebSocket through the console; no SSH port is opened on any host. Every session is audited.

commands.name: connect
commands.summary: Open psql, mysql, redis-cli or mongosh against a database through a local tunnel.
flags: Print the local URL and keep the tunnel open instead of starting a client
details: The client must be installed locally. Arguments after `--` and standard input are passed through, so `pg_dump ... | 5050 connect Postgres -- psql` works.

commands.name: domain
commands.summary: Generate a domain or add a custom domain for the linked service.
details: With no argument it generates a name under the install's base domain. With a domain it prints the DNS records to create. See [Custom domains and HTTPS](/docs/guides/custom-domains).

commands.name: tcp-proxy
commands.summary: Expose a TCP port of the linked service on a public port.
details: The public port is picked from 20000 to 29999 on every ingress host.

commands.name: environment
commands.summary: Switch, create, sync and inspect environments.
flags: Copy services, settings and non-sealed variables from ENV (staged)
Stage the edit instead of committing it
details: `config` prints the environment's effective configuration as JSON.
`edit` changes one setting, for example `deploy.replicas`, using the names in [Service settings](/docs/reference/service-settings).

commands.name: service
commands.summary: Switch the linked service or change a service.
flags: With `status`: every service in the environment

commands.name: scale
commands.summary: Set the number of replicas for the linked service.
details: The change is committed at once. A service with a volume can only run 1 replica.

commands.name: volume
commands.summary: List, add, delete or wipe the linked service's volume.
details: `wipe` stops the service, empties the volume and starts it again. You are asked to type the volume name unless `-y` is given.
Deleted volumes are kept for 48 hours before their data is removed.

commands.name: cron
commands.summary: List cron runs of the linked service or start one now.

commands.name: metrics
commands.summary: Print CPU, memory, network and HTTP summaries for the linked service.

commands.name: usage
commands.summary: Show resource usage for a period and what it would cost on Railway.
flags: Period as `YYYY-MM-DD` (default: the current period up to now)
details: The Railway estimate uses the dated list prices published with the docs site.

commands.name: config
commands.summary: Export an environment's services and settings to a file.
flags: Where to write (default `5050.yaml`; `-` for standard output)
details: The file uses the [config file schema](/docs/reference/config-file). Variables are listed by name; values are not written.
commands.railway: Railway has no direct equivalent; its `config` style sync is planned for a later 5050cloud release.

commands.name: host
commands.summary: Add, list, drain and maintain hosts.
flags: With `add`: a name for the host
details: Admin only. `add` prints a single-use join command valid for 1 hour. See [Add a host](/docs/guides/add-a-host).
commands.railway: Railway has no equivalent: hosts are its servers.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.summary: Upgrade the install: the control plane first, then each agent.
details: Admin only. The command waits and reports the result. If the new version is not healthy within 90 seconds it reverts itself. See [Upgrading](/docs/guides/upgrading).

commands.name: alias
commands.summary: Install or remove the `railway` symlink to this CLI.
details: See [The railway alias](/docs/cli/railway-alias).

commands.name: completion
commands.summary: Print a shell completion script.

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Print the CLI version.
